title: Go SDK: affinity-aware stream handoff, lease TTLs, and jittered reconnect strategy
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers see long tail failures and subtle correctness bugs when a client-side cancellation races with reconnects or when a short-lived server-side stream lease expires. Existing retry backoff is deterministic and can cause hot re-connections to the same node; KV cache warmup is wasted when session affinity is not preserved. We need a coordinated approach across the Go SDK runtime to ensure graceful client cancellation semantics, robust reconnect/backoff behavior, and efficient lease handoffs to minimize wasted work and reduce request amplification.

Goal: Implement an affinity-aware stream handoff mechanism combined with lease TTLs and a jittered, membership-aware exponential backoff so that: 1) client cancellations reliably stop in-flight work and surface the right error to callers; 2) reconnects avoid thundering herd and respect affinity to reuse warmed KV/prefetch caches where possible; 3) lease handoffs let a server return a short grace window so in-flight requests can finish or be resumed without loss.

Scope: SDK-level changes (Go client) and light server-side coordination signals (lease TTL + affinity token). Work items include:
- Add a short, opaque affinity token carried in initial stream handshake and persisted in the stream client.
- When reconnecting, prefer nodes that match affinity token for a configurable window (affinity_ttl).
- Implement lease TTL support in the SDK to signal graceful handoff windows and expose lease metadata on stream session objects.
- Replace deterministic linear backoff with jittered exponential backoff tuned for streaming: base=100ms, max=10s, random jitter +-20%, and membership-awareness to favor preferred nodes.
- Preserve context cancellation semantics: when ctx is canceled, propagate a CancelStream message and wait a short grace period (configurable) for server ack before tearing down; if server does not ack, return context.Canceled to caller.
- Introduce a 'soft-close' API for graceful drain: SDK callers can request drain-with-timeout to allow final pending tokens to flush.
- Metrics and observability: reconnection_attempts, reconnection_affinity_hit, lease_expiry_count, canceled_during_grace, average_grace_wait_ms, affinity_token_rotation.
- Tests: unit tests for backoff jitter distribution, integration tests simulating affinity-preserving reconnects, chaos tests for lease expiry during large in-flight KV cache.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Affinity improves cache reuse but can reduce load-spreading; we avoid long-lived affinity windows to prevent hotspots.
- Soft-close and ack wait introduces small latency in shutdown paths; provide knobs for customers to tune.
- Server changes are minimal: add lease_ttl and affinity_token in stream handshake metadata; fallback path exists if not provided.

Rollout plan: feature flag gated in SDK, enable for internal canary customers, collect metrics and heatmaps for affinity_hit ratio and canceled_during_grace. If affinity causes hotspots, shorten affinity_ttl and increase jitter.

Deliverables: design doc link, SDK PR, integration test harness, release notes for go-sdk-1.9.
